# Drive Move-Out

> Free, open-source web app that bulk-transfers ownership of a Google Drive folder, including every file and subfolder inside it, from one personal Google (Gmail) account to another. Nothing is downloaded or re-uploaded: the files stay where they are and only the owner changes, so they move to the new owner's storage quota.

Google Drive only lets a personal account transfer ownership one item at a time, and transferring a folder does not transfer its contents. Drive Move-Out walks the whole folder tree and transfers every item it owns, using the Drive API's pending-owner flow: the current owner invites the new owner as pending owner, then the new owner accepts.

Key facts:

- Works with personal (consumer) Google accounts only, not Google Workspace.
- Both accounts sign in in the same browser tab. Files go straight between the browser and the Google Drive API; the server only exchanges OAuth codes and stores nothing.
- Sign-in lives in the tab's sessionStorage and is revoked when the tab closes. Progress is saved in the browser (IndexedDB), so a stopped transfer resumes where it left off.
- Links, sharing settings and comments are kept. The previous owner keeps editor access.
- Items the current owner doesn't own (shortcuts, files shared by others) are skipped.
- Runs 4, 8 or 12 transfers in parallel and slows down automatically when Google rate-limits.

- [Source code and documentation](https://github.com/thaihuynhatquang/google-drive-move-out): README with setup, deployment and FAQ

- [Privacy](https://github.com/thaihuynhatquang/google-drive-move-out#privacy): what is and isn't stored
- [Limitations](https://github.com/thaihuynhatquang/google-drive-move-out#limitations): Workspace accounts, OAuth verification, rate limits
